ashcrown.doc: The Ashcrown trial (M3-C05-02; act1_ch05.md B08, SPEC 6.6 'lighting channels'; logic in AshcrownTrial). A strike caught at a tier's catch-rod charges that tier's copper bowl and lights its ring of `studs` studs. One stud goes dark for every `metres_per_stud` metres the party walks (the clock is counted in steps, never seconds: pillar 4); when the last goes dark the charge fades and is re-caught at the same tier's rod, never back at the crown. Each tier's bowl pours into `bowl_into`. A vein-gate is a bronze disc that faces outlets[rotation] (rotation 0..steps-1, one 90-degree step a turn): another gate, `spout` (the tier's downspout: the strike pours to the next tier's bowl, or on the last tier into the anvil court), `ground` (an ash drift: the charge is lost), `seal` (the sealed side vein: it opens the quench-trough alcove, sets alcove_flag, and costs the charge) or `none` (a vein to nowhere: the circuit is open and nothing runs). A gate with `linked` turns its twin with it. A `plate` gate has one fixed outlet and passes only while a party member stands on its plate (the view shows Toma there; `plate_start` is where he begins). Pulling a tier's release sends the charge along the traced path. solution_turns is the band each tier's fewest gate turns from its start must sit in (tests/unit/test_ashcrown_trial.gd). hint_scene plays once after hint_idle_sec on one tier with no turn. landed_flag is set when the last run strikes the anvil-stone.

tiers.seal_note: g3a facing 0 runs into the sealed side vein (the optional quench charm)
